Figure 1. Pediatrician attitudes about nirsevimab, Pediatrician survey, October 2024, n=200. Key: blue specifies ‘Strongly Agree or agree.’ Grey is ‘Neither agree or disagree.’ Red is ‘Disagree or strongly disagree.’ Nirsevimab is safe for infants: 96.5% Strongly agree, 3.0% Neither agree or disagree, .5% Disagree or Strongly Disagree Nirsevimab is effective against severe RSV disease in infants: 95.5% Strongly agree, 4.0% Neither agree or disagree, .5% Disagree or Strongly Disagree I feel confident discussing and recommending nirsevimab immunization with my patient’s parents/caregivers: 94.5% Strongly agree, 4.5% Neither agree or disagree, 1.0% Disagree or Strongly Disagree I feel comfortable co-administering nirsevimab and one or more vaccines to my pediatric patients in one visit: 91% Strongly agree, 7.0% Neither agree or disagree, 2.0% Disagree or Strongly Disagree.

images.alt: Figure 2. Frequency of main challenges the practice had experienced or anticipates experiencing with offering nirsevimab, Pediatrician survey, October 2024, n=200. Key: Grey color is ‘All pediatricians (n=200). Blue color is ‘Pediatricians whose practice had ever offered nirsevimab (n=154).’ Yellow color is ‘Pediatricians whose practice had never offered nirsevimab (n=46). Parent/caregiver concern around nirsevimab safety: 44.0% gray, 47.4% blue, 32.6% yellow. Challenges knowing maternal RSV vaccination status to determine infant eligibility**: 33.5% gray, 38.3% blue, 17.4% yellow. Financial burden in purchasing of nirsevimab tab  private stock of nirsevimab for practices participating in the VFC program)**: 30.5% gray, 26.0% blue, 45.7% yellow. Challenges with reimbursement from private health insurance plans: 30.5% gray, 27.9% blue, 39.1% yellow. Lack of demand from parents/caregivers**: 24.5% gray, 28.6% blue, 10.9% yellow. Challenges knowing whether infant received nirsevimab at a birthing facility to determine eligibility: 20.0% gray, 21.4% blue, 10.9% yellow. Parent/caregiver concerns around nirsevimab effectiveness: 20.0% gray, 20.1% blue, 19.6% yellow. Challengs with Medicaid reimbursement: 15.5% gray, 13.0% blue, 23.9% yellow. Supply/stock issues: 7.5% gray, 7.8% blue, 6.5% yellow. Other: 2.0% gray, 1.3% blue, 4.3% yellow. This practice does not have or does not anticipate having challenges in offering nisrevimab: 8.5% gray, 7.8% blue, 10.9% yellow.

images.alt: Figure 3. OB/GYN attitudes about maternal RSV vaccination, OB/GYN survey, October 2024, n=200. Key: blue color is ‘Strongly Agree or agree.’ Grey color is ‘Neither agree or disagree.’ Red color is ‘Disagree or strongly disagree.’ RSV vaccination during pregnancy is safe: 92.0% Strongly agree, 6.0% Neither agree or disagree, 2.0% Disagree or Strongly disagree. RSV vaccination during pregnancy is effective against severe RSV disease in infants: 93.5% Strongly agree, 6.5% Neither agree or disagree. I feel confident discussing and recommending RSV vaccination to women who are pregnant: 88.0% Strongly agree, 9.0% Neither agree or disagree, 3.0% Disagree or Strongly disagree. I feel confident discussing both RSV vaccination during pregnancy and infant nirsevimab immunization: 75.0% Strongly agree, 16.0% Neither agree or disagree, 9.0% Disagree or Strongly disagree. I feel comfortable with my patients choosing whichever RSV product they prefer: 81.0% Strongly agree, 15.5% Neither agree or disagree, 3.5% Disagree or Strongly disagree. OBGYN offices should offer RSV vaccination to pregnant women rather than referring them to another location for vaccination: 80.0% Strongly agree, 14.0% Neither agree or disagree, 6.0% Disagree or Strongly disagree.

checks.label: HTTPS (required for service workers)
checks.why: HTTPS is required for service workers and most install prompts.

checks.label: Web app manifest declared
checks.why: A web app manifest is required for installability and controls how the app appears when launched.

checks.label: Service worker registered
checks.why: A service worker is what makes offline access, caching, and background sync possible.

checks.label: Theme color declared
checks.why: Theme color controls the browser chrome/status-bar color when the site is installed or bookmarked.

checks.label: Apple touch icon (iOS/bookmark icon)
checks.why: iOS uses this icon for home-screen bookmarks and "Add to Home Screen" — without it the icon falls back to a screenshot.

checks.label: Manifest fetched and parsed successfully
checks.why: A manifest that fails to parse cannot drive installability or launch behavior even if the link is present.

checks.label: Manifest declares a maskable icon
checks.why: A maskable icon lets the OS safely crop/mask the app icon on different device shapes without clipping content.

checks.label: Service worker is active (not just registered)
checks.why: An active service worker (not just registered) is what actually intercepts requests and serves cached content.

checks.label: Service worker controls this page load
checks.why: A controlling service worker means THIS page load is being served/intercepted, not just a future one.

checks.label: Meets basic installability criteria
checks.why: Determines whether the browser can realistically offer "Add to Home Screen" / install, based on manifest + service worker + HTTPS together.
